highlights.2: Library, playlists, waveform player, and LAN access.
highlights.3: Audio editor, Demucs stem separation, and video generation.

ublock.description: A CPU- and memory-efficient content blocker focused on privacy and extensive filtering.
ublock.whyTitle: Everyday privacy should be a setting, not a subscription.
ublock.whyDescription: uBlock Origin is a concrete example of free software returning control to the user. Filters, custom rules, and dynamic mode let people decide what their browser can load and connect to.

highlights.0: Blocks ads, trackers, coin miners, popups, and malicious sites.
highlights.1: Ships with EasyList, EasyPrivacy, and other filter lists.
highlights.2: Supports custom rules and extended syntax.
highlights.3: Basic mode and a dynamic per-site filtering firewall.

quarkdown.description: A Markdown-based typesetting system for creating books, papers, knowledge bases, and presentations.
quarkdown.whyTitle: Write complex content without losing control of the format.
quarkdown.whyDescription: Quarkdown starts with the familiarity of Markdown and extends it toward paginated documents, slides, and knowledge bases. It suits anyone who wants a text-based, versionable workflow that can reach multiple formats.

highlights.0: Extends CommonMark/GFM with functions, variables, and scripting.
highlights.1: Compiles to HTML, PDF, and plain text.
highlights.2: Supports paginated documents, slides, and wiki/docs.
highlights.3: Live preview, fast builds, and a VS Code extension.

maigret.description: An OSINT tool that searches thousands of websites for accounts linked to a username and gathers public information.
maigret.whyTitle: Search public traces without jumping between a thousand sites.
maigret.whyDescription: Maigret organizes username OSINT into a repeatable workflow with an updated database, filters, and exports. It is a powerful tool to use carefully and within the rules.

highlights.0: Supports more than 3,000 websites.
highlights.1: Standard searches require no API key.
highlights.2: Recursive search, tag filters, and an updated database.
highlights.3: Web interface, multiple exports, and optional AI analysis.

pixelle-video.description: An automated AI short-video engine that turns a topic into scripts, visuals, narration, music, and a final composition.
pixelle-video.whyTitle: From a topic to a video through a composable pipeline.
pixelle-video.whyDescription: Pixelle-Video shows how different generative tools can become one workflow. Scripts, visuals, voice-over, and editing are orchestrated in a pipeline that remains extensible.

highlights.0: Automatically generates text, images, video, and voice-over.
highlights.1: Works with ComfyUI, RunningHub, and multiple API providers.
highlights.2: Includes TTS, voice cloning, and motion transfer.
highlights.3: Streamlit interface and integrated Windows package.

docuseal.description: An open-source platform for creating, filling, signing, and processing PDF documents online.
docuseal.whyTitle: Digital signatures without a closed workflow.
docuseal.whyDescription: DocuSeal brings forms and signatures into an installable, integrable platform. APIs, webhooks, and local storage let teams adapt document workflows to their own needs.

highlights.0: WYSIWYG builder for PDF forms.
highlights.1: Signatures, signature verification, and multiple signers.
highlights.2: API, webhooks, SMTP, and cloud or local storage.
highlights.3: Mobile-friendly and multilingual interface.

scrapling.description: An adaptive Python web-scraping framework covering single requests through large-scale concurrent crawling.
scrapling.whyTitle: Scraping that tries to survive changing websites.
scrapling.whyDescription: Scrapling combines HTTP requests, dynamic browsers, and concurrent crawlers in one framework. Adaptive element handling reduces maintenance when a site’s markup evolves.

highlights.0: Automatically relocates elements after structural changes.
highlights.1: HTTP fetchers, dynamic browsers, sessions, and proxy rotation.
highlights.2: Concurrent spiders with pause, resume, and streaming.
highlights.3: CLI, interactive shell, Docker, and an MCP server.

local-deep-research.description: A local, agentic AI research assistant with citations, multiple LLMs, and a searchable private knowledge base.
local-deep-research.whyTitle: AI-assisted research without giving up privacy.
local-deep-research.whyDescription: Local Deep Research brings web sources, academic research, and personal documents into a local environment. Encryption, no telemetry, and multi-model support make it a strong example of controllable technology.

highlights.0: Searches the web, academic sources, and local documents.
highlights.1: Generates summaries, analysis, and exportable reports.
highlights.2: Separate encrypted SQLCipher databases per user.
highlights.3: No telemetry, analytics, or tracking.

dflash.description: A lightweight block-diffusion model for speculative decoding, designed for efficient parallel drafting.
dflash.whyTitle: Speeding up inference by improving the draft.
dflash.whyDescription: DFlash tackles a concrete problem: producing useful parallel proposals to reduce the cost of generation. Its backends and benchmarks make it valuable for anyone studying model infrastructure.

highlights.0: Supports Qwen, Gemma, Llama, Kimi, MiniMax, and other models.
highlights.1: Transformers, SGLang, vLLM, and MLX backends.
highlights.2: Draft models published on Hugging Face.
highlights.3: Benchmarks for GSM8K, Math500, HumanEval, MBPP, and MT-Bench.

openreel-video.description: An open-source professional video editor running entirely in the browser and on the user’s device.
openreel-video.whyTitle: Edit video without uploading it to a server.
openreel-video.whyDescription: OpenReel Video is a direct example of privacy by design: editing stays in the browser and uses modern hardware APIs. It brings professional tools into a local-feeling web application.

highlights.0: Does not upload videos to external servers.
highlights.1: Multitrack timeline, effects, keyframes, and color grading.
highlights.2: WebGPU and WebCodecs hardware acceleration.
highlights.3: MP4, WebM, ProRes, audio, and image-sequence export.

lobehub.description: A workspace for creating, organizing, and coordinating AI-agent teams with memory, groups, scheduling, and automation.
lobehub.whyTitle: AI agents as a workspace, not isolated chats.
lobehub.whyDescription: LobeHub organizes agents, models, and automations in a shared working surface. Self-hosting, plugins, and gateways let individuals and teams adapt the environment to their needs.

highlights.0: Agents, schedules, reports, and messaging gateways.
highlights.1: Agent Builder for different models and modes.
highlights.2: Agent Groups, pages, projects, and shared workspaces.
highlights.3: Self-hosting through Docker, Vercel, and other providers.

agent-skills.description: A collection of production-grade workflows and skills for AI coding agents.
agent-skills.whyTitle: Give agents a process, not just a prompt.
agent-skills.whyDescription: Agent Skills collects operational instructions for moving through the development lifecycle with more discipline. Specs, planning, builds, tests, reviews, and security become reusable workflows across tools.

highlights.0: 24 skills organized across the development lifecycle.
highlights.1: Eight slash commands including /spec, /plan, /build, and /test.
highlights.2: Four personas for review, testing, security, and performance.
highlights.3: Supports Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode, Codex, and Copilot.

easy-vibe.description: An interactive learning path for turning ideas into prototypes, full-stack applications, and AI-assisted projects.
easy-vibe.whyTitle: Learn to build products with AI at your side.
easy-vibe.whyDescription: Easy-Vibe offers a gradual path from an idea to frontend, backend, databases, and deployment. Its range of levels and languages makes it a practical entry point to AI-assisted building.

highlights.0: Paths for beginners, junior developers, and advanced learners.
highlights.1: Prototyping, frontend, backend, databases, deployment, and billing.
highlights.2: Claude Code, MCP, Skills, and agent teams.
highlights.3: Ten languages and more than 80 interactive topics.

stenoai.description: A private AI notepad for recording, transcribing, summarizing, and querying confidential conversations on-device.
stenoai.whyTitle: Confidential meetings stay on your device.
stenoai.whyDescription: Steno builds a complete workflow for sensitive conversations: audio capture, transcription, summaries, and questions across a meeting library. Its on-device approach and Markdown export keep the content under the user’s control.

highlights.0: Records, transcribes, summarizes, and answers questions about meetings.
highlights.1: Live speaker labels with Parakeet on Apple Silicon.
highlights.2: Notes and transcripts saved as editable Markdown.
highlights.3: Optional OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, and custom endpoint support.

open-design.description: An open-source Claude Design alternative for creating prototypes, dashboards, decks, and media with AI agents.
open-design.whyTitle: A design studio that speaks to your agents.
open-design.whyDescription: Open Design moves the work from a closed canvas to filesystem-based skills, design systems, and plugins. The output can be a prototype, dashboard, or deck, with exports that remain useful outside the app.

highlights.0: Local-first desktop app for macOS and Windows.
highlights.1: Skills, design systems, plugins, and coding-agent integrations.
highlights.2: Prototypes, dashboards, decks, images, video, and HyperFrames.
highlights.3: Exports HTML, PDF, PPTX, MP4, ZIP, and Markdown.

supertonic.description: A fast, local multilingual text-to-speech system designed for devices and edge hardware.
supertonic.whyTitle: An AI voice without sending audio to the cloud.
supertonic.whyDescription: Supertonic brings speech synthesis directly onto the device with a compact model and multiple runtimes. It suits products that need low latency, multilingual support, and independence from the network.

highlights.0: Local synthesis across 31 languages.
highlights.1: A 99-million-parameter open-weight model.
highlights.2: Runs on desktop, mobile, browsers, Raspberry Pi, and edge hardware.
highlights.3: SDK examples for Python, Node.js, WebGPU, Java, C++, Go, Swift, Rust, and Flutter.

scrcpy.description: A lightweight tool for mirroring and controlling Android devices from Linux, Windows, or macOS.
scrcpy.whyTitle: Turn a phone into a desktop window without an app install.
scrcpy.whyDescription: scrcpy does one focused thing with very little friction: it brings Android video, audio, and control to the desktop. It needs no root, account, or internet connection, and leaves no software on the device.

highlights.0: Mirrors and controls devices over USB or TCP/IP.
highlights.1: Supports Linux, Windows, and macOS without root access.
highlights.2: Audio, recording, virtual displays, cameras, and gamepads.
highlights.3: Reported 35–70 ms latency and roughly one-second startup.

ruview.description: A WiFi sensing platform that turns radio signals into presence, movement, and vital-sign data without cameras.
ruview.whyTitle: Read a room without looking at it.
ruview.whyDescription: RuView uses CSI and ESP32 sensors to extract spatial signals from ordinary WiFi waves. Edge processing and smart-home integrations make it an unusual combination of sensing, privacy, and home automation.

highlights.0: Detects presence, movement, breathing, and heart rate.
highlights.1: Runs on edge hardware without cloud, cameras, or internet.
highlights.2: Integrates with Home Assistant, Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa, and Matter.
highlights.3: Includes a 105-module edge catalog and pretrained Hugging Face models.

supervision.description: A model-agnostic Python toolkit for building computer-vision applications and working with datasets.
supervision.whyTitle: Computer-vision building blocks without marrying one model.
supervision.whyDescription: Supervision handles the repetitive layer around models: loading data, annotating images, counting zones, and converting datasets. Its model-agnostic approach lets teams change the underlying stack without rewriting the application.

highlights.0: Building blocks from data handling to real-time zone counting.
highlights.1: Connectors for Ultralytics, Transformers, MMDetection, and Inference.
highlights.2: Highly customizable annotators for visualizations.
highlights.3: Utilities for loading, splitting, merging, and saving datasets.

shannon.description: An autonomous AI pentester that analyzes code and executes real exploits against web apps and APIs.
shannon.whyTitle: Not just alerts: vulnerabilities demonstrated with an exploit.
shannon.whyDescription: Shannon combines white-box analysis with dynamic testing to follow realistic attack paths. Its final report includes only issues backed by a proof of concept, with an explicit requirement to use it only on authorized systems.

highlights.0: Autonomous pentesting for web applications and APIs.
highlights.1: Source analysis, reconnaissance, and live exploitation.
highlights.2: Reports based on reproducible proof-of-concept attacks.
highlights.3: Resumable Docker workspaces and configurable authenticated testing.

cli-anything.description: A toolkit for making software agent-native through structured CLIs, harnesses, and an installable hub.
cli-anything.whyTitle: Give agents a universal interface to software.
cli-anything.whyDescription: CLI-Anything starts with a simple idea: discoverable, composable commands with structured output are easy for agents to use. The project combines harness generation, skills, and an installable registry.

highlights.0: Turns software into agent-ready CLIs.
highlights.1: CLI-Hub searches, installs, updates, and launches CLIs.
highlights.2: JSON and human-readable output for composable workflows.
highlights.3: A seven-phase workflow with skills for coding agents.

cal-diy.description: A community-driven, self-hosted open-source scheduling platform without commercial dependencies.
cal-diy.whyDescription: Cal.diy takes Cal.com’s core and removes enterprise and commercial code. It is built for people who want to run their own scheduling system, with MIT code and infrastructure under their control.

highlights.0: A fully open-source scheduling platform.
highlights.1: No account or license key required.
highlights.2: A self-hosted project with no managed version.
highlights.3: Next.js, tRPC, React, Tailwind, Prisma, and PostgreSQL.

listmonk.description: A fast, feature-rich self-hosted newsletter and mailing-list manager shipped as a single binary.
listmonk.whyTitle: Newsletters under your control, in one binary.
listmonk.whyDescription: listmonk focuses on operational simplicity: a standalone application, PostgreSQL as its datastore, and installation through Docker or a binary release. It is a practical base for communication without relying on a SaaS.

highlights.0: Self-hosted newsletter and mailing-list management.
highlights.1: A single binary backed by PostgreSQL.
highlights.2: Installation through Docker Compose or a binary release.
highlights.3: Go backend and Vue frontend with Buefy.

codegraph.description: Local semantic code intelligence for AI agents, with graphs of symbols, calls, and dependencies.
codegraph.whyTitle: Less grep, more of the right context.
codegraph.whyDescription: CodeGraph builds a queryable map of a codebase and keeps it synchronized as files change. The goal is to give agents structural context in a few calls instead of repeatedly crawling files by hand.

highlights.0: Local semantic intelligence for coding agents.
highlights.1: Graphs symbols, calls, dependencies, and blast radius.
highlights.2: Automatically syncs as files change.
highlights.3: MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, and more.

medusa.description: Open-source building blocks for creating customized digital-commerce applications.
medusa.whyTitle: Composable commerce instead of another monolith.
medusa.whyDescription: Medusa provides modules and a framework for building DTC stores, B2B commerce, marketplaces, and POS systems from reusable commerce primitives. Teams can customize the experience without rebuilding the foundation.

highlights.0: Building blocks for digital-commerce applications.
highlights.1: Supports DTC, B2B, marketplaces, distributors, and POS.
highlights.2: A built-in framework for customization.
highlights.3: Open-source commerce modules distributed through npm.

kronos.description: An open-source foundation model for forecasting financial candlestick sequences and market data.
kronos.whyDescription: Kronos applies hierarchical tokenizers and an autoregressive Transformer to OHLCV sequences. Its models come in different capacities for experimenting with financial forecasting and fine-tuning.

highlights.0: Trained on data from more than 45 global exchanges.
highlights.1: Quantizes OHLCV K-line data into hierarchical discrete tokens.
highlights.2: A model family from 4.1M to 499.2M parameters.
highlights.3: Models and tokenizers are available on Hugging Face.

paperless-ngx.description: A document-management system that turns physical documents into a searchable online archive.
paperless-ngx.whyTitle: Less paper without handing the archive to a SaaS.
paperless-ngx.whyDescription: Paperless-ngx organizes physical documents into a searchable digital archive you can run on your own server. Docker Compose, documentation, and a translation community make it practical to adopt and maintain.

highlights.0: Searchable online archive for physical documents.
highlights.1: Docker Compose is the recommended deployment path.
highlights.2: Official successor to Paperless and Paperless-ng.
highlights.3: Translations coordinated through Crowdin with Matrix support.

frigate.description: A local NVR for IP cameras with AI object detection and Home Assistant integration.
frigate.whyTitle: Local surveillance that understands what is happening.
frigate.whyDescription: Frigate combines an NVR, object detection, and home-automation integration without sending the video stream to a cloud. Motion detection, object-based retention, and low-latency live view keep the system focused on useful events.

highlights.0: Local object detection with OpenCV and TensorFlow.
highlights.1: Tight Home Assistant integration through a custom component.
highlights.2: 24/7 recording and retention based on detected objects.
highlights.3: MQTT, RTSP restreaming, WebRTC, and MSE live view.

twenty.description: An open-source CRM designed to be customized, extended, and versioned like the rest of your stack.
twenty.whyTitle: A CRM your team can build, ship, and version.
twenty.whyDescription: Twenty treats CRM as a platform: objects, views, workflows, and agents become composable building blocks. Its CLI and Docker Compose self-hosting fit naturally into development workflows.

highlights.0: Open-source CRM built for technical teams.
highlights.1: Objects, views, workflows, and agents as building blocks.
highlights.2: CLI for creating and publishing custom apps.
highlights.3: TypeScript stack with NestJS, React, PostgreSQL, and Redis.

krawl.description: A cloud-native web honeypot using deceptive pages, fake credentials, and canary tokens to detect attacks.
krawl.whyTitle: Waste scanners’ time while you watch.
krawl.whyDescription: Krawl builds decoy web surfaces with fake panels, credentials, and paths to distinguish legitimate crawlers from malicious activity. It can run standalone or scale behind Kubernetes.

highlights.0: Deception pages, fake logins, honeypot paths, and canary tokens.
highlights.1: Real-time dashboard with IP insight and attack types.
highlights.2: Standalone SQLite or scalable PostgreSQL and Redis modes.
highlights.3: Deployment through Docker, Kubernetes, and Helm.

heretic.description: An automatic tool for removing safety alignment from transformer language models.
heretic.whyTitle: Alignment research from the command line.
heretic.whyDescription: Heretic automates directional ablation and optimizes parameters to reduce refusals while preserving as much of the original model’s behavior as possible. It is a research tool that requires care when interpreting models and results.

highlights.0: Combines directional ablation with Optuna’s TPE optimizer.
highlights.1: Supports dense, multimodal, MoE, and some hybrid models.
highlights.2: Can save, upload, chat with, and benchmark generated models.
highlights.3: Includes research features for residuals and internal geometry.

markitdown.description: A lightweight Python utility for converting documents and media to Markdown for LLM workflows.
markitdown.whyTitle: Bring heterogeneous documents into the format LLMs understand well.
markitdown.whyDescription: MarkItDown prioritizes structure and content over visual fidelity. Its CLI, Python API, and optional dependencies turn many formats into Markdown ready for analysis and AI pipelines.

highlights.0: Converts PDF, PowerPoint, Word, Excel, images, and audio.
highlights.1: Supports HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, ZIP, YouTube, and EPUB.
highlights.2: CLI and Python API with local or stream conversion.
highlights.3: Optional plugins for OCR, transcription, and Azure services.

stirling-pdf.description: An open-source PDF platform for editing, signing, redacting, converting, and automating documents locally.
stirling-pdf.whyTitle: PDF tools that stay inside your infrastructure.
stirling-pdf.whyDescription: Stirling PDF brings editing, conversion, and automation into an application you can run on desktop, in the browser, or on your own servers. Its private API and no-code workflows extend it beyond manual use.

highlights.0: More than 50 tools for working with PDFs.
highlights.1: Desktop client, browser interface, and self-hosted server.
highlights.2: No-code pipelines and REST APIs for PDF processing.
highlights.3: Interface available in more than 40 languages.

microsoft-activation-scripts.description: Open-source Windows and Office activation scripts featuring HWID, Ohook, TSforge, and Online KMS methods.
microsoft-activation-scripts.whyTitle: System automation with one rule first: verify the source.
microsoft-activation-scripts.whyDescription: MAS collects activation methods and troubleshooting in publicly distributed scripts. Its README emphasizes checking URLs and the risks of unofficial copies.

highlights.0: HWID, Ohook, TSforge, and Online KMS methods.
highlights.1: PowerShell entry point and traditional CMD script.
highlights.2: Declared support from Windows Vista onward.
highlights.3: Homepage, troubleshooting, and malware warnings for altered copies.

voxcpm.description: A tokenizer-free multilingual text-to-speech system for natural speech, voice design, and controllable cloning.
voxcpm.whyTitle: Synthetic speech that does not start from discrete tokens.
voxcpm.whyDescription: VoxCPM generates continuous speech representations through a diffusion autoregressive architecture. VoxCPM2 combines languages, voice design, cloning, and 48kHz audio in a model usable through Python and compatible serving options.

highlights.0: The 2B-parameter VoxCPM2 model supports 30 languages.
highlights.1: Voice design from a natural-language description.
highlights.2: Controllable and ultimate cloning from reference audio.
highlights.3: 48kHz output and real-time streaming with vLLM options.

ecc.description: An operating system for AI-agent workflows, with skills, memory, hooks, MCP configurations, and security scanning.
ecc.whyTitle: An operating system for everyday agentic work.
ecc.whyDescription: ECC collects operational practices from multi-harness workflows: skills, persistent memory, verification, orchestration, and security. The same foundation adapts across coding-agent CLIs and environments.

highlights.0: Skills, hooks, rules, memory, and MCP configurations.
highlights.1: Works across Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, Zed, and Copilot.
highlights.2: Guides for token optimization, evaluations, and parallelization.
highlights.3: Security-scanning surfaces and AgentShield included.

flowsint.description: An open-source OSINT tool for visually exploring entities, relationships, and investigation enrichments.
flowsint.whyTitle: OSINT as a graph to explore, not a list of results.
flowsint.whyDescription: Flowsint connects domains, IPs, organizations, social accounts, and other signals in a visual interface. Self-hosting keeps investigation data on the machine while enrichers use local infrastructure services.

highlights.0: Visual graph for relationships between entities.
highlights.1: Enrichers for DNS, WHOIS, social, breaches, email, and websites.
highlights.2: Local storage with an explicit privacy focus.
highlights.3: Docker deployment with PostgreSQL, Redis, Neo4j, and Nginx.

last30days-skill.description: An agent-led search engine synthesizing recent signals from social, news, research, and markets.
last30days-skill.whyTitle: Search what people are doing, not what editors have indexed.
last30days-skill.whyDescription: /last30days crosses different sources and weighs signals through engagement, citations, and context. The result is an updated brief for people, topics, companies, trends, and comparisons.

highlights.0: Reddit, X, YouTube, TikTok, GitHub, arXiv, and more.
highlights.1: Ranks upvotes, likes, comments, views, and market signals.
highlights.2: Runs on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and Gemini CLI.
highlights.3: Cited briefs, comparisons, discovery mode, and historical lookbacks.

spec-kit.description: An open-source toolkit for turning product specifications into executable software-development workflows.
spec-kit.whyTitle: Define the outcome before writing the code.
spec-kit.whyDescription: Spec Kit makes the specification an operational artifact: principles, requirements, plans, tasks, and implementation become explicit phases. Its CLI connects the path to many coding agents.

highlights.0: Spec-driven workflow for high-quality software.
highlights.1: Specify CLI for initializing projects and integrations.
highlights.2: Commands for constitution, specify, plan, tasks, and implement.
highlights.3: Integrations with more than 30 AI coding agents.

trivy.description: A versatile security scanner for containers, filesystems, Git repositories, virtual machines, and Kubernetes clusters.
trivy.whyTitle: One scanner for many risk surfaces.
trivy.whyDescription: Trivy brings vulnerability, SBOM, configuration, secret, and license scanning into a CLI for images, repositories, and clusters. Integrations place it directly inside development and deployment workflows.

highlights.0: Scans images, filesystems, Git, VMs, and Kubernetes.
highlights.1: Finds CVEs, dependencies, SBOM, IaC, secrets, and licenses.
highlights.2: Installable through Homebrew, Docker, or binaries.
highlights.3: GitHub Actions, Kubernetes operator, and VS Code integrations.

career-ops.description: An AI command center for evaluating job offers, tailoring CVs, and managing a career search.
career-ops.whyTitle: Run a job search like a system, not an endless spreadsheet.
career-ops.whyDescription: Career-Ops uses agents and browser automation to filter opportunities, research companies, and prepare targeted materials. It keeps a human in control: the agent recommends, but never submits applications.

highlights.0: Offer evaluation with scoring across ten dimensions.
highlights.1: ATS-optimized tailored CV PDFs.
highlights.2: Scans Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever, Wellfound, and company portals.
highlights.3: Batch processing, TUI dashboard, and human-in-the-loop workflows.

tolaria.description: A desktop app for portable, offline-first Markdown knowledge bases that work with AI workflows.
tolaria.whyTitle: A knowledge base that does not lock you into an app.
tolaria.whyDescription: Tolaria treats notes as Git-versioned Markdown files readable by standard tools. The result is a local workspace suited both to personal thinking and to context for AI agents.

highlights.0: Markdown notes with YAML frontmatter.
highlights.1: Git-first, offline-first vaults without lock-in.
highlights.2: Setup paths for Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI.
highlights.3: Tauri app for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

goose.description: A native open-source AI agent for code, research, writing, automation, and data analysis, available as an app, CLI, and API.
goose.whyTitle: A general agent that lives on your machine.
goose.whyDescription: goose takes agent workflows beyond coding: its desktop app, CLI, and API cover research, writing, automation, and analysis. Multiple providers and MCP extensions keep the infrastructure choice open.

highlights.0: Desktop app, CLI, and API for macOS, Linux, and Windows.
highlights.1: More than 15 providers and 70+ MCP extensions.
highlights.2: API keys and existing subscriptions through ACP.
highlights.3: A native agent built in Rust.

whichllm.description: A CLI that finds local LLMs that can actually run on your hardware.
whichllm.whyTitle: Choose a model based on the machine you really have.
whichllm.whyDescription: whichllm detects GPU, CPU, and RAM, then ranks Hugging Face models that appear suitable for the system. It can simulate hardware configurations and distinguish what fits from what runs well.

highlights.0: Detects hardware and ranks compatible models.
highlights.1: Simulates GPUs and multi-GPU workstations.
highlights.2: Filters by VRAM, speed, and headroom.
highlights.3: CLI, Markdown, JSON, and Python snippet output.

fluxer.description: A free, open-source instant-messaging and VoIP chat app for friends, groups, and communities.
fluxer.whyTitle: Community chat without a proprietary platform fence.
fluxer.whyDescription: Fluxer is a free messaging and VoIP app for conversations between friends, groups, and communities. Its API and self-hosting documentation are being finalized as its audio and video systems evolve.

highlights.0: Instant messaging and VoIP chat.
highlights.1: Designed for friends, groups, and communities.
highlights.2: Canary client already available on the web and for download.
highlights.3: API and self-hosting documentation in progress.

restic.description: A fast, efficient, secure backup program with encrypted and deduplicated snapshots.
restic.whyTitle: Backup that treats restore as the most important part.
restic.whyDescription: restic combines encryption, deduplication, and verifiable snapshots in a cross-platform program. Backends range from local directories and SFTP to S3, cloud services, and rclone.

highlights.0: Backup and restore on Linux, macOS, Windows, FreeBSD, and OpenBSD.
highlights.1: Encryption for confidentiality and integrity.
highlights.2: Incremental snapshots with deduplication.
highlights.3: Local, SFTP, REST, S3, Azure, GCS, and rclone backends.

aisuite.description: A Python library with unified APIs for LLM chat and agents with tools, toolkits, and MCP.
aisuite.whyTitle: Switch providers without rewriting application logic.
aisuite.whyDescription: aisuite standardizes chat completions and tool calling across providers through one Python interface. On top of the library, OpenCoworker demonstrates a desktop agent that can perform real tasks.

highlights.0: Chat Completions API with an OpenAI-style interface.
highlights.1: Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Ollama, and more.
highlights.2: Agents API for Python functions, toolkits, and MCP servers.
highlights.3: OpenCoworker for research, files, deliverables, and local automation.

cypress.description: A fast, reliable testing framework for anything that runs in a browser.
cypress.whyTitle: Test the browser without turning every test into infrastructure.
cypress.whyDescription: Cypress focuses the testing experience on browser applications and offers simple installation through common JavaScript package managers. Cypress Cloud completes the loop with shareable badges and results.

highlights.0: Browser testing for Mac, Linux, and Windows.
highlights.1: Installable through npm, Yarn, or pnpm.

0.title: Clarify the real business constraint

1.title: Select the minimum viable architecture

2.title: Connect models, interfaces, and data flows
